method.description: Opened the exact supplied files, expanded the signature root, inspected the full visible Signatures panel, opened native Signature Properties, clicked Validate Signature, and transcribed the resulting messages. H and I2 were each closed, reopened and explicitly revalidated a second time; their results repeated.
method.propertyTranscription: Literal message text with surrounding whitespace removed. The full status line includes signing time and source of trust. Decorative images, memory addresses, dialog controls and generic section titles are omitted.
method.changeCategories: No modification-category rows were displayed in the expanded Signatures panel for any of the nine files. This is a UI observation, not a claim about hidden internal categories.
method.screenshots: Inspected interactively; no standalone observation screenshots saved.

interpretation.observed: With both signer identities trusted, G and H are VALID and unchanged; A, B2-F2 and I2 are INVALID with altered/corrupted wording. The H/I2 results repeated on reopen and explicit revalidation.
interpretation.trustHypothesis: Missing signer trust is not sufficient to explain these rejections: all failing results include valid signer identity and manually imported trust.
interpretation.viewerSpecificHypothesis: A signing revision produced by the viewer is not necessary to trigger the failure: I2 also fails after the supplied pyHanko-signed H control.
interpretation.remainingScope: The shared ebook and its interaction with incremental updates are the leading area to investigate. The exact cause is not isolated; common appended-revision construction remains a possible factor. These results do not prove that the base itself is malformed, nor that all PDFs signed by the viewer fail after later edits.
interpretation.round1Limit: The defective B-F round-1 files are not reused as evidence that an unrelated rewrite or orphan append must fail. This run uses the corrected B2-F2 inputs and preserves the old observations separately.
